t: For carrying out the provisions of title 23, United States Code, which are attributable to Federal-aid highways, to remain available until expended, $4,155,370,000, or so much thereof as may be available in and derived from the “Highway trust fund”; which sum is composed of $587,218,731, the balance of the amount authorized for the fiscal year 1967, and $3,552,518,466 (or so much thereof as may be available in and derived from the “Highway trust fund”), a part of the amount authorized to be appropriated for the fiscal year 1968, $15,499,136 for reimbursement of the sum expended for the repair or reconstruction of highways and bridges which have been damaged or destroyed by floods, hurricanes, or landslides, as provided by title 23, United States Code, section 125, and $133,667 for reimbursement of the sums expended for the design and construction of bridges upon and across dams, as provided by title 23, United States Code, section 320.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriation for Federal-aid highways drawn from the Highway Trust Fund, itemizing amounts and reimbursements. A tempting reading is that Federal-aid highways imply coordination with states, but the text sets out no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: For carrying out the provisions of title 23, United States Code, which are attributable to Federal-aid highways, to remain available until expended, $4,155,370,000, or so much thereof as may be available in and derived from the “Highway trust fund”

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes the spending of specific sums of money for federal-aid highways. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) in making decisions. It merely allocates funds.
qwen_block.s: For carrying out the provisions of title 23, United States Code, which are attributable to Federal-aid highways, to remain available until expended, $4,155,370,000, or so much thereof as may be available in and derived from the “Highway trust fund”

opus.w: This section only appropriates money from the Highway Trust Fund for Federal-aid highways and reimbursements under title 23. It does not mention any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. The mentions of "reimbursement" and of states' highway spending might look like outside involvement, but they only describe how the funds are made up, not any outside role in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation clause that authorizes the spending of specific sums of money for highway construction and repairs. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making a decision. The mention of 'Federal-aid highways' refers to the program being funded, not to a participatory decision-making process within this text.
qwen_chat.s: For carrying out the provisions of title 23, United States Code, which are attributable to Federal-aid highways, to remain available until expended, $4,155,370,000, or so much thereof as may be available in and derived from the “Highway trust fund”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for "Federal-aid highways," which involve state governments, there is implicit participation. However, the text itself is purely an appropriation clause specifying dollar amounts and sources of funds. It does not describe any process of consultation, coordination, or decision-making involving outside parties. The reference to Title 23 is merely to identify the statutory authority for the expenditure, not to invoke a participation mechanism within this specific section.
